metadata.title: Nobody Is Coming to Approve It.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro af_bella) - per-beat mp3 durations are MEASURED, never estimated
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: French (Salut). Ep. 03 used Hej, Ep. 04 Ciao, Ep. 05 Ola; no language repeats within the series.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 06 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, built from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 06 (Mars rover autonomy - how AI lets rovers choose their own driving path and interesting rock targets without waiting on Earth). Per the series notes in ideas.md, Ep. 01 already established the data-volume premise, so this episode does not re-argue it. The premise here is not volume at all: it is LATENCY. The expert is between 3 and 22 light-minutes away and the sol ends whether or not anyone answered.
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is the ONE accent and marks exactly one committed decision per beat: the chosen path, the chosen rock, the driven route, the frozen profile. Terrain plates are monochrome camera frames - Navcam and Hazcam really are greyscale instruments, so the mono plate is the honest depiction. Cost maps are ink-on-white grids, deliberately unlike the plates, because a cost map is a data product and not a picture.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Ep. 03 ended on out-of-distribution failure, Ep. 04 on the crowd ceiling, Ep. 05 on irreversibility. Ep. 06 is about none of those: the premise is that the decision cannot WAIT for review, because review is up to 22 light-minutes away in each direction and the sol is over before an answer arrives. The two limits are correspondingly new - autonomy buys distance by spending distance (759 m driven to cover 520 m straight-line), and the rover's definition of interesting is frozen between software uplinks (AEGIS-Lite sol 442 to AEGIS-Heavy sol 697, 255 sols apart).
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, with RESULT lines), B11 (verdict artifact), B12 (handoff), B13 (title outro). Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). All terrain plates are SYNTHETIC, generated by assets/gen_mars.py from a seeded procedural height field, and captioned as synthetic wherever a viewer could mistake them for a NASA image. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the same GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03's BUILD-LOG. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE: the same file lays out for 16:9 and for the 9:16 derivative in short/.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about how a Mars rover chooses its own route and its own rocks, without waiting for Earth. It has to — a question can take twenty-two minutes each way.

show.event: cream page; IRREDUCIBLY HUMAN eyebrow, then the serif segment title Nobody Is Coming to Approve It
spark + greeting Salut, HAI settles above the composer card
the ask types itself into the composer; send button arms when it lands
terracotta running indicator: the uplink window is closing...
three result lines stagger in - method, accuracy, limit. The ask lands ANSWERED.

props.segment: Nobody Is Coming to Approve It
props.command: A Mars rover gets one plan a sol and the round trip to Earth can be 44 minutes. What is the actual method it uses to choose a route and a science target on its own, how good is it, and what does that autonomy cost?
output: method - score a fan of candidate paths on a terrain cost map; score rocks on a profile written on Earth
accuracy - about 90% of Perseverance's driving is autonomous, against 6.2% for Curiosity
limit - caution is paid in metres, and the definition of interesting is frozen between uplinks

beats.narration_text: This is Humanitarians AI. Every episode so far was about too much data. This one is about distance.

show.event: top-left kicker: AI IN ASTRONOMY & SPACE SCIENCE - EP. 06
the name OM MALI draws on large, terracotta hairline sweeping under it
role line fades in beneath: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a second panel sets two rows: 'every episode so far: too much data' struck through, then 'this one: too much distance' with the accented token
@HumanitariansAI wordmark bug settles bottom-right, inside title-safe

beats.narration_text: One breath. A rover gets one plan a day. Whatever that plan missed, it settles alone — scoring paths against a map of the ground, and rocks against a definition of interesting written before launch.

show.event: kinetic type, set one: ONE PLAN A DAY, over a faint navcam plate
set two: TWO DECISIONS - where to drive, what to look at - as two chips
set three: SCORED, NOT ASKED, the accented token landing on SCORED
closer: nobody is coming to approve it

beats.narration_text: Here's the number that forces everything. A signal takes three to twenty-two minutes to cross from Mars, and as long again for an answer. So there's no joystick — the rover runs commands written yesterday.

show.event: two discs, Earth left and Mars right, a long horizontal channel between them
a terracotta pulse travels the channel; a bracket labels it 3 to 22 minutes, one way
the pulse returns; the bracket doubles to 'up to 44 minutes for an answer'
a struck-through joystick chip: NO REAL-TIME CONTROL
a sol bar fills below: ONE COMMAND BLOCK, UPLINKED BEFORE THE ROVER WAKES
closer: an unanswered question costs a day

beats.narration_text: What does it work from? Two cameras give a stereo view, which becomes a height map. Then it throws almost all of that away, leaving a grid of cells, each holding one number: how rough the ground is.

show.event: the synthetic navcam plate lands left, framed, captioned SYNTHETIC
a second, slightly offset plate slides behind it - the stereo pair
an arrow crosses to the right: the cost grid draws on cell by cell
one cell is called out with a terracotta ring and two labels: STEP HEIGHT, SLOPE
closer: one number per cell is the whole world

beats.narration_text: Now the choice. Perseverance imagines about seventeen hundred paths six metres ahead, scoring each on time and roughness. Most run through something it can't cross. It clearance-checks the few left and drives the best, while the wheels turn.

show.event: the cost grid fills the figure band; the rover mark sits bottom-centre
the candidate fan draws on: ~1,700 PATHS chip, 6 m horizon bracket
rejected arcs grey out as a REJECTED label lands
the survivors darken; a CLEARANCE CHECK chip lands on them
exactly one arc turns terracotta and a ring lands on its waypoint
a second-computer chip: IT LOOKS WHILE IT DRIVES

beats.narration_text: The science side is the same move. AEGIS finds edges, groups them into closed outlines, measures size, brightness and distance, then ranks them against a profile of what matters here. The top rock gets the laser.

show.event: the rockfield plate lands large, captioned SYNTHETIC
it cross-fades to the contour version: closed outlines draw on around six rocks
three measurement chips stagger beside it: SIZE, BRIGHTNESS, RANGE
a SCENE PROFILE card slides in, listing what the science team asked for
the ranked plate replaces it: one contour is terracotta
closer: the laser fires without asking

beats.narration_text: Here's what that buys. In 2023 Perseverance crossed a boulder field called Snowdrift Peak. Straight across was five hundred and twenty metres; it drove seven hundred and fifty-nine, in six days — twelve days faster than Curiosity.

show.event: the top-down route map lands, framed and captioned SCHEMATIC
the grey straight line is labelled 520 m STRAIGHT ACROSS
the terracotta driven route is labelled 759 m ACTUALLY DRIVEN
two counters land beside it: 6 SOLS, and ~12 SOLS SAVED
closer: it went further to get there sooner

beats.narration_text: Now the design tell. The rover doesn't decide what's interesting. It applies a definition geologists wrote on Earth, in advance: big, bright, close, this shape. The taste is a document, and it has an author.

show.event: a document card draws on centre: SCENE PROFILE, with four rule lines
each line types: prefer LARGE, prefer BRIGHT, prefer NEAR, prefer THIS OUTLINE
a signature line at the foot of the card: WRITTEN ON EARTH, BEFORE LAUNCH, in the accented token
an arrow carries the card across the light-time gap to the rover mark
closer: the taste is a document, and it has an author

beats.narration_text: The numbers are good. Curiosity drove six percent of its distance autonomously; Perseverance, near ninety. Its longest unreviewed drive was almost seven hundred metres. AEGIS hit the intended material over ninety-three percent of the time, against twenty blind.

show.event: two stacked bars draw on: CURIOSITY 6.2%, PERSEVERANCE ~90%, autonomous share of distance
a distance rule lands beneath: 699.9 m, longest drive with no human review
right panel, two more bars: AEGIS >93%, BLIND POINTING ~20%, both labelled
citation line names the two sources and the conditions

beats.narration_text: Two limits, neither a bug. Caution is paid in metres — two hundred and thirty-nine of those Snowdrift metres went around things. And you can only change its mind on a mission clock: sol four forty-two, then six ninety-seven.

show.event: left panel: the route map again, reduced; a terracotta bracket marks the 239 m of detour
label beneath it: CAUTION, PAID IN METRES
right panel: a sol axis draws on, two ticks land - SOL 442 and SOL 697
the span between them fills terracotta and reads 255 SOLS
label beneath: ONE DEFINITION OF INTERESTING, THEN THE NEXT
closer: you can only change its mind on a mission clock

beats.narration_text: Recap. Distance, not volume, forces the autonomy. Driving is a scored fan of paths over a roughness grid. Science is outlines ranked against a profile written on Earth. The cost: extra metres, and the wait to change its mind.

show.event: the artifact page scales up on the cream stage, spark + title bar
four numbered recap lines stagger in, one per spoken clause

props.artifactTitle: Nobody Is Coming to Approve It - one page
props.artifactHeading: The method, and what it costs
artifactLines: The forcing constraint is latency, not volume: 3-22 minutes each way, and one command block per sol.
Driving: stereo images become a grid of roughness numbers; ~1,700 candidate paths are scored over ~6 m.
Science: edges are grouped into closed outlines, measured, and ranked against a profile written on Earth.
The cost: 759 m driven to cover 520 m - and 255 sols between one definition of interesting and the next.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this. I'm designing a system that must judge before any human reviews it. Help me write its criteria, set how conservative it should be when being wrong is asymmetric, and plan how to update it after deployment. Grade it: arguable criteria, priced conservatism, a way to change its mind.

show.event: spark + greeting 'Your turn.' - the one greeting that drops the persona
the suggested prompt types itself into the composer while the voice reads it verbatim
terracotta running line: paste this into Claude...
the three-item rubric staggers in as output lines, one per spoken grading criterion
